hypothesis: Does the small recurrent result survive an established Hugging Face real-text benchmark with official held-out splits and a stronger Transformer baseline?
split: Official train/validation/test files; original text rows joined with one LF, encoded UTF-8 without normalization, truncation, or unknown-token substitution
tokenization: lossless UTF-8 bytes, fixed vocabulary 256; bpb not directly comparable with v7 bpc
recurrent_width: nearest total parameter count to transformer selected before training
optimizer: Adam beta1 .9 beta2 .999 epsilon 1e-8; global grad norm clip 1
selection: One tuning seed101 per each of three learning rates, select full validation bpb; save selection before accessing test scores
evaluation: All complete 64-byte segments of each official held-out split; state resets every64 bytes; last incomplete segment excluded and exact scored token counts disclosed; token-weighted loss
stopping: 400 steps every run, no early stopping or best-seed selection
limits: Equal parameter/token/tuning budgets do not mean equal FLOPs. Tiny undertrained models, short context and one dataset do not measure intelligence, frontier equivalence or business economics. No model selection against test loss.
